(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Site plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Site plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Site plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Site plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | Latitude_deg = 35| Latitude_min = 1| Latitude_sec = 33.45 | Longitude_deg = 135| Longitude_min = 40| Longitude_sec = 46.70 | ISO = JP-26 | Shape = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳]] | Dimensions = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Site plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}: Small urn (1), necked jar fragments. == See Also == * {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | Latitude_deg = 35| Latitude_min = 1| Latitude_sec = 33.45 | Longitude_deg = 135| Longitude_min = 40| Longitude_sec = 46.70 | ISO = JP-26 | Shape = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳]] | Dimensions = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Site plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}: Small urn (1), necked jar fragments. == See Also == * {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun (Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | Latitude_deg = 35| Latitude_min = 1| Latitude_sec = 33.45 | Longitude_deg = 135| Longitude_min = 40| Longitude_sec = 46.70 | ISO = JP-26 | Shape = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳]] | Dimensions = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Site plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * {{Infobox ancient site | name = Maruyama Kofun | image = [[File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-1.jpg|280px]]
Tumulus
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | Latitude_deg = 35| Latitude_min = 1| Latitude_sec = 33.45 | Longitude_deg = 135| Longitude_min = 40| Longitude_sec = 46.70 | ISO = JP-26 | Shape = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳]] | Dimensions = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue ware|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji ware|ja|土師器]] | Burial Mounds = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Site plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue ware (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial Mausoleum Reference Site," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}.
