(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} | name = Maruyama Kofun | image = [[File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-1.jpg|280px]]
Kofun
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | Latitude_deg = 35| Latitude_min = 1| Latitude_sec = 33.45 | Longitude_deg = 135| Longitude_min = 40| Longitude_sec = 46.70 | ISO = JP-26 | Shape = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | Dimensions = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-2.jpg|Kofun File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), sekizai.jpg|Stone materials on the mound File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), entrance.jpg|Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}}: Small urn (1), necked jar fragments. == See Also == * {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}} * {{ill|Maruyama Kofun|ja|円山古墳}} * {{ill|Kitsunezuka Kofun (Kyoto)|ja|狐塚古墳 (京都市)}} * {{ill|Kitsunezuka Kofun (Kyoto City)|ja|狐塚古墳 (京都市)}} == Notes == {{Reflist}} == References == {{small|Sources used in the article:}} * Published by the Imperial Household Agency ''' {{Cite book|ja|author={{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}}|year=2001|chapter={{PDFlink|[https://shoryobu.kunaicho.go.jp/Publication/PDF/000/kiyo053b001.pdf Maruyama and Nyudozuka Imperial Mausoleum Reports]}}|title=Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|publisher=Imperial Household Agency}} * Published by Local Governments ''' {{Cite book|ja|author=|year=1976|chapter=Overview of Daikakuji Kofun Group Excavations|title=Kyoto Archaeological Reports|publisher=Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education}} * Encyclopedias ''' {{Cite book|ja|author=Marukawa Yoshihiro|year=2002|chapter=Daikakuji Kofun Group|title=Encyclopedia of Japanese Kofun|publisher=Tokyodo Shuppan}} * Others ''' {{Cite journal|ja|author={{ill|Hanakuma Yuki|ja|花熊祐基}}|title=Daikakuji 4th Kofun Excavation and Survey Report|date=2016|journal=Ryukoku University This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} | name = Maruyama Kofun | image = [[File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-1.jpg|280px]]
Kofun
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | Latitude_deg = 35| Latitude_min = 1| Latitude_sec = 33.45 | Longitude_deg = 135| Longitude_min = 40| Longitude_sec = 46.70 | ISO = JP-26 | Shape = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | Dimensions = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | Construction Period = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | Map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | Label = Maruyama Kofun | Label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-2.jpg|Kofun File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), sekizai.jpg|Stone materials on the mound File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), entrance.jpg|Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}}: Small urn (1), necked jar fragments. == See Also == * {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}} * {{ill|Maruyama Kofun|ja|円山古墳}} * {{ill|Kitsunezuka Kofun (Kyoto)|ja|狐塚古墳 (京都市)}} * {{ill|Kitsunezuka Kofun (Kyoto City)|ja|狐塚古墳 (京都市)}} == Notes == {{Reflist}} == References == {{small|Sources used in the article:}} * Published by the Imperial Household Agency ''' {{Cite book|ja|author={{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}}|year=2001|chapter={{PDFlink|[https://shoryobu.kunaicho.go.jp/Publication/PDF/000/kiyo053b001.pdf Maruyama and Nyudozuka Imperial Mausoleum Reports]}}|title=Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. Reports|publisher=Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education}} * Encyclopedias ''' {{Cite book|ja|author=Marukawa Yoshihiro|year=2002|chapter=Daikakuji Kofun Group|title=Encyclopedia of Japanese Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its scale and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}: Kofun
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | Latitude_deg = 35| Latitude_min = 1| Latitude_sec = 33.45 | Longitude_deg = 135| Longitude_min = 40| Longitude_sec = 46.70 | ISO = JP-26 | Shape = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Imperial Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label Position = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-2.jpg|Kofun File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), sekizai.jpg|Stone materials on the mound File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), entrance.jpg|Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}: Small urn (1), necked jar fragments. == See Also == * {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}} * {{ill|Maruyama Kofun|ja|円山古墳}} * {{ill|Kitsunezuka Kofun (Kyoto)|ja|狐塚古墳 (京都市)}} * {{ill|Kitsunezuka Kofun (Kyoto City)|ja|狐塚古墳 (京都市)}} == Notes == {{Reflist}} == References == {{small|Sources used in the article:}} * Published by the Imperial Household Agency ''' {{Cite Reports]}}|title=Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|publisher=Imperial Household Agency}} * Published by Local Governments ''' {{Cite book|ja|author=|year=1976|chapter=Overview of Daikakuji Kofun Group Excavations|title=Kyoto Archaeological Reports|publisher=Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education}} * Encyclopedias ''' {{Cite book|ja|author=Marukawa Yoshihiro|year=2002|chapter=Daikakuji Kofun Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Kofun
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates_deg = 35| coordinates_min = 1| coordinates_sec = 33.45 | coordinates_deg = 135| coordinates_min = 40| coordinates_sec = 46.70 | ISO = JP-26 | Shape = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | Burial Facility = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historical Site = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}: The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | other_designation = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | other_designation = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == Burial Facility == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | other_designation = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | other_designation = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}: Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Kofun
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates_deg = 35| coordinates_min = 1| coordinates_sec = 33.45 | coordinates_deg = 135| coordinates_min = 40| coordinates_sec = 46.70 | ISO = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | other_designation = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | Artifacts = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Buried Individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | other_designation = | Tangible Cultural Property = | Notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | Icon = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} plaque == Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu
