(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | other_designation = | Tangible Cultural Property = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially other_designation1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | other_designation = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially other_designation1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | other_designation = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially other_designation1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Kofun
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-2.jpg|Kofun File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), sekizai.jpg|Stone materials on the mound File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), entrance.jpg|Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-2.jpg|Kofun File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), sekizai.jpg|Stone materials on the mound File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), entrance.jpg|Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) *
