(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-2.jpg|Kofun File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), sekizai.jpg|Stone materials on the mound File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), entrance.jpg|Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) (Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft|12=draft}}, Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-2.jpg|Kofun File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), sekizai.jpg|Stone materials on the mound File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), entrance.jpg|Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-2.jpg|Kofun File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), sekizai.jpg|Stone materials on the mound File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), entrance.jpg|Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}: Small urn (1), necked jar fragments. == See Also == * {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}} * {{ill|Maruyama Kofun|ja|円山古墳}} * {{ill|Kitsunezuka Kofun revision.text:
{{日本の古墳 |名称 = 円山古墳 |画像 = [[File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-1.jpg|280px]]
墳丘
（手前は[[京都府立北嵯峨高等学校]]グラウンド） |別名 = 大覚寺1号墳/丸山古墳 |所属 = [[大覚寺古墳群]] |所在地 = [[京都府]][[京都市]][[右京区]]嵯峨大覚寺門前登リ町 |緯度度 = 35|緯度分 = 1|緯度秒 = 33.45 |経度度 = 135|経度分 = 40|経度秒 = 46.70 |ISO = JP-26 |形状 = [[円墳]] |規模 = 直径50m
高さ9.1m |埋葬施設 = 両袖式[[横穴式石室]]
（内部に組合式[[家形石棺]]2基） |出土品 = [[装飾付大刀]]・耳環・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[6世紀]]後半 |被葬者 = （[[宮内庁]]推定）[[正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|正子内親王]] |陵墓 = [[宮内庁]]治定「円山陵墓参考地」 |史跡 = |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図 = Japan Kyoto city |アイコン = 円墳 |ラベル = 円山古墳 |ラベル位置 = bottom }} {{OSM Location map | coord = {{Coord|35|1|29.8|N|135|40|50.0|E}} | zoom = 16 | float = right | width = 300| height =250 | caption = {{center|大覚寺古墳群分布図}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1= {{Coord|35|1|33.45|N|135|40|46.70|E}} | label1=1号墳（円山） | label-pos1=top | label-color1=black | mark1=円墳.png | mark-size1=30 | mark-coord2= {{Coord|35|1|31.63|N|135|40|53.04|E}} | label2=2号墳（入道塚） | label-pos2=top | label-color2=black | mark2=方墳.png | mark-size2=30 | mark-coord3= {{Coord|35|1|29.00|N|135|40|49.02|E}} | label3=3号墳（南天塚） | label-pos3=top | label-color3=black | mark3=円墳.png | mark-size3=30 | mark-coord4= {{Coord|35|1|26.17|N|135|40|54.70|E}} | label4=4号墳（狐塚） | label-pos4=top | label-color4=black | mark4=円墳.png | mark-size4=30 }} '''円山古墳'''（まるやまこふん、大覚寺1号墳）は、[[京都府]][[京都市]][[右京区]]嵯峨大覚寺門前登リ町にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。[[大覚寺古墳群]]を構成する古墳の1つ。 実際の被葬者は明らかではないが、[[宮内庁]]により「'''円山陵墓参考地'''」（被葬候補者：第53代[[淳和天皇]][[皇后]][[正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|正子内親王]]）として[[陵墓参考地]]に治定されている。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+[[大覚寺古墳群]]一覧{{Sfn|花熊祐基|2016}} !順!!古墳名!!形状!!規模!!築造時期!!陵墓・史跡 |- |1||'''1号墳
（円山古墳）'''||[[円墳]]||直径50m||6c後半||[[陵墓参考地]] |- |2||3号墳
（南天塚古墳）||円墳|| ||6c後半-末||（埋没） |- |rowspan=2|3||[[狐塚古墳 (京都市)|4号墳
（狐塚古墳）]]||円墳||直径28m||rowspan=2|7c初頭-前半||なし |- |2号墳
（入道塚古墳）||[[方墳]]||25×30m|||陵墓参考地 |}
[[京都盆地]]（山城盆地）西部の[[有栖川]][[扇状地]]に築造された大型円墳である。一帯では4基の古墳が分布して大覚寺古墳群を形成し、本古墳はそのうち最北端に位置する。[[1951年]]（[[昭和]]26年）に石室の発掘調査が実施され（調査後に石室は閉塞）、[[1975年]]（昭和50年）に墳丘周囲の発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は円形で、直径50メートル・高さ9.1メートルを測る{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。墳丘は2段築成{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。墳丘外表で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められていない{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。墳丘周囲には幅13メートルの周濠が巡らされるが、墳丘南側（石室正面）では途切れて幅約2.7メートルの陸橋を形成する{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]で、南方向に開口した。石室全長14.7メートルを測る大型石室であり、太秦・嵯峨野地域では[[蛇塚古墳]]に次ぐ規模になる{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。石室内には少なくとも2基の竜山石製の組合式[[家形石棺]]が据えられる。石室内からは、副葬品として耳環・環頭大刀把頭（[[装飾付大刀]]）・馬具・[[須恵器]]（TK43型式期）・[[土師器]]などが検出されている。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]後半頃と推定される{{Sfn|花熊祐基|2016}}。大覚寺古墳群では最初に築造された古墳として位置づけられ、墳丘規模・石室規模・副葬品のいずれも有力氏族の首長像を示唆する古墳として注目される。実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[淳和天皇]][[皇后]]の[[正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|正子内親王]]（[[879年]]死去）の墓とする伝承があり、現在は[[陵墓参考地]]に治定されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1899年]]（[[明治]]32年）、宮内省（現・[[宮内庁]]）により[[陵墓参考地]]に治定[[外池昇]]「円山陵墓参考地」『事典陵墓参考地 もうひとつの天皇陵』吉川弘文館、2005年。。 * [[1951年]]（[[昭和]]26年）、石室の発掘調査。副葬品出土、調査後に石室は閉塞（[[小林行雄]]ら、[[2001年]]に報告）{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第53号|2001}}。 * [[1975年]]（昭和50年）、[[京都府立北嵯峨高等学校]]建設に伴う墳丘周囲の発掘調査（京都府教育委員会、[[1976年]]に報告）{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設としては両袖式[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、南方向に開口した。石室の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|花熊祐基|2016}}。 * 石室全長：14.7メートル * 玄室：長さ5.4メートル、幅3.2メートル、高さ4.5メートル * 羨道：長さ9.3メートル、幅2.0メートル、高さ2.4メートル 玄室の奥壁は各段1石の3段積みである。側壁は各段2石の2-3段積みで、目地が通る。羨道は大型の基底石の上に2石を積む{{Sfn|花熊祐基|2016}}。 玄室内には、奥壁寄りと入り口寄りに少なくとも2基の竜山石製の組合式[[家形石棺]]が据えられる。奥壁寄りの石棺蓋石には長辺に各2個の縄掛突起が、入り口寄りの蓋石には長辺各2個・短辺各1個の縄掛突起が認められ、入り口寄りの方が古い型式とされる{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。 File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-2.jpg|墳丘 File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), sekizai.jpg|墳丘上の石室石材 File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), entrance.jpg|円山陵墓参考地駒札 == 出土品 == 石室内の発掘調査で検出された副葬品は次の通り{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第53号|2001}}。 * 金環 2 * 環頭把頭 2 * 金銅鞘金具片 1 * 鉄刀片 1 * 鉄刀子片 1 * 鉄鏃片 1 * 金銅辻金具片 4 * [[須恵器]] - 壺1、壺蓋1、𤭯2、瓶子1、小型瓶子1。 * [[土師器]] - 坩1、長頸壺片。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 宮内庁発行 ** {{Cite book|和書|author=[[小林行雄]]|year=2001|chapter={{PDFlink|[https://shoryobu.kunaicho.go.jp/Publication/PDF/000/kiyo053b001.pdf 円山陵墓参考地・入道塚陵墓参考地調査報告]}}|title=書陵部紀要 第53号|publisher=[[宮内庁書陵部]]|ref={{Harvid|書陵部紀要 第53号|2001}}}} - リンクは宮内庁「書陵部所蔵資料目録・画像公開システム」。 * 地方自治体発行 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1976|chapter=大覚寺古墳群発掘調査概要|title=埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報（1976）|publisher=京都府教育委員会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}}} * 事典類 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=丸川義広|year=2002|chapter=大覚寺古墳群|title=[[日本古墳大辞典|続 日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|大覚寺古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1979|chapter=円山塚|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 27 京都市の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4-582-49027-5|ref={{Harvid|円山塚（平凡社）|1979}}}} * その他 ** {{Cite book|和書|author=[[広瀬和雄]]|year=2013|chapter=山城・蛇塚古墳をめぐる二,三の問題|title=国立歴史民俗博物館研究報告 第178集|publisher=[[国立歴史民俗博物館]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|広瀬和雄|2013}}}} ** {{Cite journal|和書|author=花熊祐基|title=大覚寺4号墳第2次発掘・測量調査報告 > 考察|date=2016|journal=龍谷大学考古学実習|publisher=龍谷大学文学部考古学実習室|volume=|number=12|pages=|url=|naid=|doi=|ref={{Harvid|花熊祐基|2016}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite journal|和書|author=|title=丸山古墳・入道塚|date=1962|journal=とれんち|publisher=京都大学考古学研究会|volume=|number=2|pages=|url=|naid=|doi=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[京都大学]]考古学研究会|author=|year=1971|chapter=各古墳の概要 > 丸山古墳|title=嵯峨野の古墳時代 -御堂ヶ池群集墳発掘調査報告-|publisher=京大考古学研究会出版事務局|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=京都市|author=|year=1983|chapter=古墳時代 > 右京区|title=史料京都の歴史 第2巻 考古|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|史料京都の歴史 第2巻 考古|1983}}}} == 関連項目 == {{Commonscat|Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto)}} * [[大覚寺古墳群]] {{DEFAULTSORT:まるやまこふん きようとし}} [[Category:太秦・嵯峨野古墳群]] [[Category:京都府の古墳]] [[Category:右京区の歴史]] [[Category:円墳]] [[Category:陵墓参考地]] [[Category:太秦]]

[[京都盆地]]（山城盆地）西部の[[有栖川]][[扇状地]]に築造された大型円墳である。一帯では4基の古墳が分布して大覚寺古墳群を形成し、本古墳はそのうち最北端に位置する。[[1951年]]（[[昭和]]26年）に石室の発掘調査が実施され（調査後に石室は閉塞）、[[1975年]]（昭和50年）に墳丘周囲の発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は円形で、直径50メートル・高さ9.1メートルを測る{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。墳丘は2段築成{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。墳丘外表で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められていない{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。墳丘周囲には幅13メートルの周濠が巡らされるが、墳丘南側（石室正面）では途切れて幅約2.7メートルの陸橋を形成する{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]で、南方向に開口した。石室全長14.7メートルを測る大型石室であり、太秦・嵯峨野地域では[[蛇塚古墳]]に次ぐ規模になる{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。石室内には少なくとも2基の竜山石製の組合式[[家形石棺]]が据えられる。石室内からは、副葬品として耳環・環頭大刀把頭（[[装飾付大刀]]）・馬具・[[須恵器]]（TK43型式期）・[[土師器]]などが検出されている。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]後半頃と推定される{{Sfn|花熊祐基|2016}}。大覚寺古墳群では最初に築造された古墳として位置づけられ、墳丘規模・石室規模・副葬品のいずれも有力氏族の首長像を示唆する古墳として注目される。実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[淳和天皇]][[皇后]]の[[正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|正子内親王]]（[[879年]]死去）の墓とする伝承があり、現在は[[陵墓参考地]]に治定されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1899年]]（[[明治]]32年）、宮内省（現・[[宮内庁]]）により[[陵墓参考地]]に治定[[外池昇]]「円山陵墓参考地」『事典陵墓参考地 もうひとつの天皇陵』吉川弘文館、2005年。。 * [[1951年]]（[[昭和]]26年）、石室の発掘調査。副葬品出土、調査後に石室は閉塞（[[小林行雄]]ら、[[2001年]]に報告）{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第53号|2001}}。 * [[1975年]]（昭和50年）、[[京都府立北嵯峨高等学校]]建設に伴う墳丘周囲の発掘調査（京都府教育委員会、[[1976年]]に報告）{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設としては両袖式[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、南方向に開口した。石室の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|花熊祐基|2016}}。 * 石室全長：14.7メートル * 玄室：長さ5.4メートル、幅3.2メートル、高さ4.5メートル * 羨道：長さ9.3メートル、幅2.0メートル、高さ2.4メートル 玄室の奥壁は各段1石の3段積みである。側壁は各段2石の2-3段積みで、目地が通る。羨道は大型の基底石の上に2石を積む{{Sfn|花熊祐基|2016}}。 玄室内には、奥壁寄りと入り口寄りに少なくとも2基の竜山石製の組合式[[家形石棺]]が据えられる。奥壁寄りの石棺蓋石には長辺に各2個の縄掛突起が、入り口寄りの蓋石には長辺各2個・短辺各1個の縄掛突起が認められ、入り口寄りの方が古い型式とされる{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}。 File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), funkyu-2.jpg|墳丘 File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), sekizai.jpg|墳丘上の石室石材 File:Maruyama Kofun (Kyoto), entrance.jpg|円山陵墓参考地駒札 == 出土品 == 石室内の発掘調査で検出された副葬品は次の通り{{Sfn|埋蔵文化財発掘調査概報|1976}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第53号|2001}}。 * 金環 2 * 環頭把頭 2 * 金銅鞘金具片 1 * 鉄刀片 1 * 鉄刀子片 1 * 鉄鏃片 1 * 金銅辻金具片 4 * [[須恵器]] - 壺1、壺蓋1、𤭯2、瓶子1、小型瓶子1。 * [[土師器]] - 坩1、長頸壺片。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 宮内庁発行 ** {{Cite book|和書|author=[[小林行雄]]|year=2001|chapter={{PDFlink|[https://shoryobu.kunaicho.go.jp/Publication/PDF/000/kiyo053b001.pdf 円山陵墓参考地・入道塚陵墓参考地調査報告]}}|title=書陵部紀要 第53号|publisher=[[宮内庁書陵部]]|ref={{Harvid|書陵部紀要 第53号|2001}}}} - (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. (With two assembled [[house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}} | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}" by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, {{ill|Ukyo-ku, Kyoto|ja|右京区|12=draft}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|12=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|12=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|12=draft|12=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''," hypothesizing {{ill|Princess Masako|ja|正子内親王 (嵯峨天皇皇女)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}} nor {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|ja|蛇塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. At least two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}} by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Site|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|house-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}.
