Kofun
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]] | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}" by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikakuji Kofun Group|qq=}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}'''," hypothesizing [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]], consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Basin|qq=}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arisugawa River|qq=}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] nor [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the [[:en:Hebizuka Kofun|Hebizuka Kofun]]. At least two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}} by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sotoike Noboru|qq=}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobayashi Yukio|qq=}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south. (With two assembled [[House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]] | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}" by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikakuji Kofun Group|qq=}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}'''," hypothesizing [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]], consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Basin|qq=}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arisugawa River|qq=}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] nor [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the [[:en:Hebizuka Kofun|Hebizuka Kofun]]. At least two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}} by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sotoike Noboru|qq=}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobayashi Yukio|qq=}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Kofun
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]] | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}" by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikakuji Kofun Group|qq=}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}'''," hypothesizing [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]], consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Basin|qq=}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arisugawa River|qq=}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] nor [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the [[:en:Hebizuka Kofun|Hebizuka Kofun]]. At least two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}} by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sotoike Noboru|qq=}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobayashi Yukio|qq=}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south. (Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]] | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}" by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikakuji Kofun Group|qq=}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}'''," hypothesizing [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]], consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Basin|qq=}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arisugawa River|qq=}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] nor [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the [[:en:Hebizuka Kofun|Hebizuka Kofun]]. At least two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}} by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sotoike Noboru|qq=}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobayashi Yukio|qq=}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]]: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]]: Small urn (1), necked jar fragments. == See Also == * {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Kofun
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]] | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}" by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikakuji Kofun Group|qq=}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}'''," hypothesizing [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]], consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Basin|qq=}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arisugawa River|qq=}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[:en:1951|1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[:en:1975|1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] nor [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the [[:en:Hebizuka Kofun|Hebizuka Kofun]]. At least two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}} by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sotoike Noboru|qq=}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobayashi Yukio|qq=}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south. Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]] | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}" by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikakuji Kofun Group|qq=}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}'''," hypothesizing [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]], consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Basin|qq=}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arisugawa River|qq=}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[:en:1951|1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[:en:1975|1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] nor [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the [[:en:Hebizuka Kofun|Hebizuka Kofun]]. At least two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}} by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sotoike Noboru|qq=}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobayashi Yukio|qq=}} in [[2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[:en:1976|1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]]: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]]: Small urn (1), necked jar fragments. == See Also == * {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun (Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]] | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}" by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikakuji Kofun Group|qq=}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}'''," hypothesizing [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]], consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Basin|qq=}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arisugawa River|qq=}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[:en:1951|1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[:en:1975|1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] nor [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the [[:en:Hebizuka Kofun|Hebizuka Kofun]]. At least two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}} by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sotoike Noboru|qq=}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobayashi Yukio|qq=}} in [[:en:2001|2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[:en:1976|1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south. Kofun
(Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]] | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}" by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikakuji Kofun Group|qq=}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}'''," hypothesizing [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]], consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Basin|qq=}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arisugawa River|qq=}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[:en:1951|1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[:en:1975|1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] nor [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the [[:en:Hebizuka Kofun|Hebizuka Kofun]]. At least two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[:en:879|879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}} by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sotoike Noboru|qq=}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobayashi Yukio|qq=}} in [[:en:2001|2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[:en:1976|1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]]: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]]: Small urn (1), necked jar fragments. == See Also == * {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun (Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]] | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}" by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikakuji Kofun Group|qq=}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}'''," hypothesizing [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]], consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Basin|qq=}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arisugawa River|qq=}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[:en:1951|1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[:en:1975|1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] nor [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the [[:en:Hebizuka Kofun|Hebizuka Kofun]]. At least two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[:en:879|879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}} by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sotoike Noboru|qq=}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobayashi Yukio|qq=}} in [[:en:2001|2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[:en:1976|1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south. (Foreground: Ground of [[Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School]]) | Other names = Daikakuji 1st Kofun / Maruyama Kofun | Part of = [[Daikakuji Kofun Group]] | location = [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho | coordinates = 35| coordinates = 1| coordinates = 33.45 | coordinates = 135| coordinates = 40| coordinates = 46.70 | omitted = JP-26 | type = [[Circular tumulus (empun)|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun]] | area = Diameter: 50m
Height: 9.1m | burial = Double-sleeved [[corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber]]
(With two assembled [[House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺]]) | burial goods = [[Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀]]・Earrings・Horse gear・[[Sue pottery|ja|須恵器]]・[[Haji pottery|ja|土師器]] | Kofuns = | built = Late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] | Interred_individual = (Estimated by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]] | Mausoleum = Designated as "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}" by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] | Historic Site = | Tangible designation1 = | notes = | map = Japan Kyoto city | type = 円墳 | map_dot_label = Maruyama Kofun | map_dot_label = bottom }} '''Maruyama Kofun''' (円山古墳, Daikakuji 1st Kofun) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Saga Daikakuji Monzen Noboricho, [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]], Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. The kofun is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and one of the tumuli composing the {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun Group|ja|大覚寺古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikakuji Kofun Group|qq=}}. The actual individual interred in this kofun is not definitively known, but the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}'''," hypothesizing [[:en:Princess Seishi|Empress Masako]], consort of Emperor Junna, as a potential burial candidate. == Overview == This large circular tumulus is located in the western part of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Basin|qq=}}, within the {{ill|Arisugawa River|ja|有栖川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arisugawa River|qq=}} alluvial fan. The Daikakuji Kofun Group consists of four tumuli distributed in the area, with Maruyama Kofun positioned as the northernmost. The stone chamber was excavated in [[:en:1951|1951]] (Showa 26) and later sealed, while the surrounding mound area was investigated in [[:en:1975|1975]] (Showa 50). The tumulus measures 50 meters in diameter and 9.1 meters in height{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The mound is constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Neither [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] nor [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were observed on the surface of the mound{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. A 13-meter-wide moat surrounds the mound, except for a land bridge approximately 2.7 meters wide on the southern side, aligned with the stone chamber's entrance{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening to the south. Measuring 14.7 meters in total length, it is among the largest stone chambers in the Uzumasa and Sagano region, second only to the [[:en:Hebizuka Kofun|Hebizuka Kofun]]. At least two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone are placed within the chamber. Excavation yielded grave goods, including earrings, decorated sword pommels, horse gear, and Sue pottery (TK43 type){{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}. The kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. As the earliest of the Daikakuji Kofun Group, its map_size and the grave goods indicate it belonged to a prominent regional leader. While the actual buried individual is unknown, local tradition associates it with Princess Masako, consort of Emperor Junna, who died in [[:en:879|879]]. The site is officially Historic Site1 as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}}. == Excavation History == * '''1899 (Meiji 32):''' Designated as an {{ill|Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial {{ill|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum}} by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]{{ill|Sotoike Noboru|ja|外池昇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sotoike Noboru|qq=}}, "Maruyama Imperial {{ill|Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}," 2005.. * '''1951 (Showa 26):''' Excavation of the stone chamber. Grave goods were discovered, and the chamber was sealed post-investigation (Reported by {{ill|Kobayashi Yukio|ja|小林行雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobayashi Yukio|qq=}} in [[:en:2001|2001]]){{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}. * '''1975 (Showa 50):''' Excavation of the mound's surrounding area due to the construction of Kyoto Prefectural Kitano Saga High School (Reported in [[:en:1976|1976]] by Kyoto Prefecture Board of Education){{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. == burial == The burial facility is a double-sleeved {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Hanakuma Yuki|2016}}: * Total Length: 14.7 meters * Main Chamber: Length 5.4 meters, Width 3.2 meters, Height 4.5 meters * Entrance Passage: Length 9.3 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 2.4 meters The main chamber features a three-tiered stone rear wall. Two assembled {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped Sarcophagus|lt=House-shaped stone coffins|ja|家形石棺|1=House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/house-shaped stone coffins|13=User:Immanuelle/House-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}} made of Ryuzan stone were placed inside, with distinct patterns on the lid stones indicating different types and periods{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}. Imperial Mausoleum|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}} plaque == burial goods == burial goods recovered from the stone chamber include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Reports|1976}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Memoirs Vol. 53|2001}}: * Gold earrings (2) * Decorated sword pommels (2) * Fragments of gilt-bronze scabbard fittings (1) * Iron sword fragments (1) * Iron knife fragments (1) * Iron arrowhead fragments (1) * Gilt-bronze fittings for bridles (4) * [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]]: Pot (1), lid (1), jar (2), flask (1), small flask (1) * [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]]: Small urn (1), necked jar fragments. == See Also == * {{ill|Daikakuji Kofun
